text:
Alice: Seeing a big spike in 502s and retries for gpu-serving in us-west-2. Grafana shows traffic funneling to 2 pods, other replicas basically idle. Kube-proxy is in ipvs mode on this cluster. Anyone seen something like this recently?

infra-bot: alert: service/gpu-serving error-rate increased 12% (5m). p50 latency 120ms -> 450ms.

Ben: Can you paste the endpoints + ipvs table from one of the nodes experiencing it? Also which kube-proxy version?

Alice: pasted outputs below from gpu-node-07 (trimmed):
``` 
$ kubectl get endpoints gpu-serving -o wide
NAME          ENDPOINTS                             AGE
gpu-serving   10.3.45.12:8080,10.3.46.33:8080,...    15d
```
```
# ipvsadm -L -n
IP Virtual Server version 1.2.1 (size=4096)
Prot LocalAddress:Port Scheduler Flags
  -> RemoteAddress:Port           Forward Weight ActiveConn InActConn
TCP  10.3.40.10:8080 rr
  -> 10.3.45.12:8080              Masq     1      12345      2
  -> 10.3.46.33:8080              Masq     1      79         0
  -> 10.3.47.14:8080              Masq     1      0          0
  -> 10.3.48.55:8080              Masq     1      5          0
```
(you can see two servers getting almost all packets)

Carla: That looks like classic IPVS hashing skew. We hit similar behaviour last year when some hosts had different MTU/GRO settings and ECMP was creating asymmetric hashing states. Do we have jumbo frames / RDMA in this region?

Alice: Some of the GPU nodes were set to MTU 9000 for RDMA (RoCE) but the ToR was 1500 on a subset of racks after a rollout. Noted RDMA is enabled on some NICs.

Dinesh: If RDMA/RoCE bypasses parts of the stack or changes L2/L3 handling, IPVS hashing can end up routing flows unevenly. Also conntrack sticky entries can bias flows. Can you check conntrack counts and ipvs persistent entries?

Ben: Quick checks to try:
- `conntrack -L | grep <svc-ip>` to find long-lived mappings
- `ipvsadm --save > /tmp/ipvs.before` then restart kube-proxy on one node and `ipvsadm --save > /tmp/ipvs.after` to compare
- `ip link show` to check MTU mismatch

Alice: Ran `ip link` across nodes: some gpu-0x nodes show mtu 9000, others 1500. Also saw `ethtool -k` differences: GRO/TCP segmentation offload enabled on some hosts, disabled on others.

Carla: That's a red flag. MTU mismatch + offload differences + ECMP next-hops -> asymmetric packetization. IPVS (which hashes 5-tuple) can see different packet stream boundaries and conntrack/ipvs updates then get skewed. Workarounds we've used:
- Temporarily set `--ipvs-scheduler=rr` (round-robin) for kube-proxy, which evens short-lived connections better.
- Disable offloads on affected NICs: `ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off` for testing.
- Make MTU consistent (preferred long-term).

Dinesh: Also check for known kube-proxy bug: when ipvs uses `sh` or `lah` schedulers combined with asymmetric ECMP, you can get persistent skew, fixed in later kube-proxy versions. Post the kube-proxy version and open issue link?

Ben: There's an open issue with IPVS unequal hashing + MTU/ECMP interactions: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/1234567 (looks similar). Patch landed in kube-proxy v1.25.2+ but some clusters need manual restart to pick new ipvs state.

Alice: What we did last: cordoned + drained gpu-node-07, restarted kube-proxy (`systemctl restart kube-proxy`), then checked `ipvsadm -L -n`. Traffic redistributed across endpoints. Also toggled ipvs scheduler to `rr` via kube-proxy args (temporary).

Ben: Good. For remediation plan:
- Short term: rollout kube-proxy restart across nodes in us-west-2 during the 0200-0400 UTC window, set `--ipvs-scheduler=rr` as a fallback flag.
- Medium: normalize MTU to 9000 or 1500 cluster-wide (decide after infra input).
- Medium: ensure NIC offload settings consistent (`ethtool -k`).
- Medium/Long: check RDMA/RoCE config on ToRs; disable RoCE on nodes that don't need it or get consistent ToR config.

Carla: Another useful diagnostic: `tcpdump -i <iface> -s0 -w capture.pcap host <svc-ip>` then look at packet sizes/fragmentation and ECMP flows. We found many fragmented flows on the path where MTU dropped.

Alice: Action items for us:
- Dinesh: file infra ticket to standardize MTU and check ToR RDMA config (assigned).
- Ben: prepare kube-proxy restart playbook and impact notes.
- Carla: run offload/ethtool audit script across GPU fleet and list mismatches.

Dinesh: filing infra ticket now and will include ToR config owners.

Ben: I'll schedule kube-proxy restart runbook and prepare rollback (save ipvs tables, drain small batches).

Alice: After the node restarts, error rate dropped back to baseline and pods got traffic evenly. We'll follow up with infra ticket results and consider full cluster restart of kube-proxy if infra changes MTU. Thanks all :thumbsup:

infra-bot: incident-note: mitigated by kube-proxy restarts and node drain. Monitoring to watch for 24h.

Carla: TL;DR - root cause likely MTU / offload mismatch + RDMA/ECMP path asymmetry exposing an IPVS hashing bug. Workarounds: scheduler change, kube-proxy restart, normalize MTU, disable offloads or RDMA until ToR config is consistent.

Alice: I'll update the incident doc with commands we ran and the ipvs diffs. Will ping once infra ticket lands.
